newsitem.title: USA: Tribune radio station to be managed by Emmis.
newsitem.headline: Tribune radio station to be managed by Emmis.

text.p: Tribune Co said it signed a contract to have Emmis Broadcasting Corp manage WQCD, an FM radio station in New York.

Under the agreement, Emmis Broadcasting will manage the station for up to three years, after which Emmis has the right to purchase the station for an undisclosed amount. During the management contract, Tribune will seek to identify a suitable property to be acquired in an exchange transaction.
The transaction becomes effective upon regulatory approval.

"Current management has done an excellent job in building the market share of WQCD," Dennis FitzSimons, president Tribune Broadcasting Co, said in a statement. "But given the rapid consolidation of the New York radio marketplace and the number of multi-station owners, we view this transaction as an opportunity to generate excellent value for 'QCD as well as value for our shareholders."
Tribune said it remains committed to ownership of its four other radio stations: WGN-AM in Chicago and KOSI-FM, KEZW-AM, and KKHK-FM in Denver.
Emmis Broadcasting Chairman Jeff Smulyan said the potential acquisition fits well with his company's strategy for growth.

"We've said all along that we will make prudent acquisitions where we can improve our existing stations and our position in our current markets," he said, adding that the WQCD agreement fits all criteria, allowing Emmis to complement the two top-rated New York stations the company already owns.
